editorial:
Fox Film Corporation released this ten-reel adaptation on February 11, 1925. Rowland V. Lee directed it, from a script by Robert N. Lee. Edward Hearn plays Lieutenant Philip Nolan, Pauline Starke plays Anne Bissell and Richard Tucker plays Aaron Burr. It is a silent historical drama built on Edward Everett Hale's patriotic story of an officer who renounces his country. Warner Bros. made a separate 1937 Technicolor short, directed by Crane Wilbur, which is a different work.

The print is free to reuse because the film was published in 1925, so its US term has run out. The rights trap is that Silent Era lists the film's survival as unknown. We found no archive copy to reuse. Any score added to a future copy would be a separate protected recording.
faq: Is the 1925 Fox film The Man Without a Country in the public domain?
The film itself is. It was published in 1925, so its US term has ended. A score on a particular copy, or other added material, may not be free.
Can I use a Man Without a Country video found online?
Check the year and studio first. Other films share this title, including a separate 1937 Warner Bros. short. We found no copy of the 1925 Fox film to link.
